_note: The COST analog of complexity-budget.json — set at project START and guard it as the design grows, with `python tools/cost/check_cost.py --game games/<slug>` and the bg-architect agent. FUN FIRST: this budget is a SOFT guardrail, not a design constraint — a fun game beats a cheap one, and most cost can be recovered LATER (crowdfunding, a higher price tier, or swapping deluxe bits for cardboard standees/punchboard) without touching the design. So during DESIGN, only push back on cost when it's genuinely running away (a cost explosion, not a needed component); otherwise let the design earn its components and optimise the bill of materials at the production stage. Fewer UNIQUE component TYPES is still the biggest lever (each type = its own tooling/assembly/QC), then box size (freight + tariff), then piece count — worth knowing, not worth strangling the fun over. Busting the budget has honest outcomes: cut/merge back under IF it doesn't cost fun, or consciously (and log-ably) accept a higher price tier / thinner margin / later-savings plan. `target_cogs_fraction` = manufactured unit cost as a fraction of retail (indie POD ~0.5; a healthy pitch/crowdfund target ~0.2). `unit_cost_per_type` are ROUGH at-volume figures (USD, pre-freight, pre-tariff) — re-verify with a live manufacturer quote before pricing. Tighten for a small-box filler; loosen freely for a bigger boxed game. See knowledge/cost-and-manufacturability.md.
